title: Clustering with K-Means & Gaussian Mixtures
summary: K-means and Gaussian mixtures both alternate between assigning points to clusters and updating the clusters. Learn the vectorized distance matrix behind both, k-means++ seeding, empty-cluster repair, and why the EM E-step must run in log space.
takeaways: Compute all point-to-centre distances at once with ||x||² − 2x·c + ||c||², broadcasting an (n,1) column against a (1,k) row.
Lloyd's algorithm never increases inertia, but it only finds a local minimum, so seed it with k-means++.
An empty cluster's mean is 0/0 = NaN. Re-seed it on the worst-explained point instead.
A GMM's E-step is a softmax over components. Compute it with logsumexp, or far-away points produce NaN.

steps.label: Seed
steps.detail: k-means++: each new centre is sampled with probability ∝ squared distance to the nearest existing centre.

steps.label: Distance matrix
steps.detail: D = ||x||² − 2·X Cᵀ + ||c||², shape (n, k), clipped at 0.

steps.label: Assign / E-step
steps.detail: K-means takes argmin per row. A GMM takes a log-space softmax over components.

steps.label: Update / M-step
steps.detail: Recompute means (and weights and variances for a GMM), repairing empty clusters.

steps.label: Check convergence
steps.detail: Stop when centroids stop moving or the log-likelihood stops improving.

terms.definition: The k-means objective: the sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid.
The standard k-means loop: assign points to the nearest centroid, then move each centroid to its points' mean.
Seeding that samples each new centre with probability proportional to its squared distance from the nearest chosen centre.
r_ij, the posterior probability that mixture component j generated point i.
Expectation–Maximization: alternate computing responsibilities (E) and re-estimating parameters (M). The likelihood never decreases.
log Σ exp(a) computed as m + log Σ exp(a − m) with m = max(a), which avoids overflow and underflow.
